title: Asking the cluster
summary: The machine arbitrator never moves a task: it asks the cluster for cross-arbitration (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25). ASK_CLUSTER is planned when a demand cannot fit here (resident RAM, local disk, fabric space, or no disk for the swap it needs), or when a higher-priority demand is blocked by a lower-priority running task: then the plan asks to move that task and the new START_TASK is WAITING. The cluster's answer arrives as an event; the arbitrator re-plans (the moved task then stops here and the waiting one starts).
authority: built and tested offline (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-25)
invariants: The arbitrator asks; it never stops a task to make room on its own
A running task keeps its place until the cluster moves it
procedure: Treat the cluster's answer as an event and call plan again
